recipes.name: Hungarian Lentil Soup
ingredients_raw: 1.5 cups lentils - soaked, rinsed and drained

steps.text: Heat oil in a large stockpot. Sauté onions until they are glossy. Stir in carrots, celery, garlic, and paprika, and sauté for 10 minutes.

Stir in chicken stock, tomatoes, lentils, bay leaves, salt, and pepper. Stir well, then add wine and bring the mixture to a boil. Slowly reduce the heat and cook for 1 hour on low to medium heat; or until lentils are tender.
Sprinkle soup with Parmesan and parsley before serving.

raw_recipe.headline: Hungarian Lentil Soup
raw_recipe.description: A lentil soup recipe with onions, garlic, carrots, celery, tomatoes, paprika and bay leaves to flavor this comforting dish that is easy to make.

review.reviewBody: I have made this recipe at least ten times and am finally making a review. I have settled on those small black lentils. You can also use WAY MORE lentils than what is mentioned here. I let them soak for about 4 hours, or overnight, it does not matter. If you do not have crushed tomatoes, tomato sauce works fine. I save money by using dried parsley because it is so expensive to buy it fresh where I live. They make you buy a huge bundle of it. Thanks for the recipe! Also, this is HUGE: It tastes WAY WAY WAY better the 2nd day. If you eat it fresh out of the pan, it is so-so, but if you put it in a big jar and eat it the next day, Mmmmmm.......

Good and pretty simple! I made half the recipe but added an extra quarter to half cup of lentils. Also I chopped rather than diced my carrots and celery and used low sodium chicken broth and red wine. I precooked red lentils the day before but still simmered an hour to thicken. I forgot the paprika but sprinkled red pepper flakes with the salt-and pepper. I also needed to add more oil as the veggies sautéed. I grated Romano cheese over my bowl and added a liberal amount of chopped parsley. Versatile recipe but basic is super- Thanks!

Third attempt to enter review since I’m tech challenged. WONDERFUL SOUP! Made some changes: Used about 10 cups stock and at least two of them were beef stock, all low salt. Increased amount of garlic, spices, and veggies by about 1/2 more. Used twice as many lentils. Used the 13 lentil variety that has almost every lentil you can think of. Soaked them and that reduced cooking time, but I also cooked it a little longer anyway. Each day this soup just got better and better! This is one soup that is hard to mess up. I think I will add cabbage next time. It freeze well also, especially with a Food Saver that will vaccum seal the air out.

This soup is hearty and tasty, but the lentils were quite hard, even after soaking them all night and simmering the soup for 2 1/2 hours. I will try what other reviewers suggested and wait until the lentils are soft before adding the tomatoes and wine. Cubes of ham are a nice addition to the soup.

Delicious dish with a little doctoring for bolder and layered flavoring. I added an additional 1/2 tsp salt along with 1 tsp basil, 1 tsp oregano, 1/2 tsp cayenne pepper and 1/2 tsp red pepper flakes. Yum!
I also sautéed the vegetables and put it all in a crock pot on high for 5 hours. My house smelled delicious when I walked in.

I used 2 containers of chicken brother instead of 7 cups because I knew I would be adding more to it. I added tomatoes 40 minutes into the lentils cooking so that the lentils would cook first. I also added peas, spinach, corn, mushrooms, sausage and Lawry's seasoned salt. I then let everything simmer for about 10 minutes. Served with parmesan. So healthy and delicious!

The 3 stars is for this recipe as is. With so much acids from the tomatoes & wine, the lentils remain somewhat firm no matter how long you cook them. I fixed this by blending the soup up. Also that much acid requires some sweetness to offset (just like any other tomato based sauce.) I added a drip of honey to my bowl, because that's what was at the table. It was much better, so I went back to the pot and added a tsp of sugar. If I make it again, I would reduce the amount of wine & hold it back along with tomatoes untill the lentils are cooked, and add 1 tsp of sugar.

This soup is SO good!!! I could eat it every day. It's exceptionally healthy too. I did make a few changes... I used one more carrot, one more stalk of celery, another teaspoon of paprika, and used diced tomatoes instead of crushed. I don't think any of those changes changed the flavor much, just made it a bit heartier. I also added some kale because I had it on hand and I love it! I definitely will make this often!
I added 1/2 pound cooked Italian sweet sausage, frozen sweet corn and Hatch medium hot green Chile. Fabulous!

Changes made: cooked in a crock pot for 12 hours. Added diced chunks of double smoked ham. And when serving add vinegar to your bowl to taste.

great recipe. Duplicates what my grandmother used to make.

I just made this soup. I had all the ingredients in the freezer so I thawed and made the soup. I put the onions and carrots in the food processor then followed all the directions but added the following. 5 large leaves of collards and 1/2 tsp of cumin. The cumin was a great addition as it added extra flavor, also I added three cups of dark lentils as I had to use up what was cooked. Soup came great thanks for the recipe
Added some chilli powder, onion powder, 1/2 cup salsa ( medium heat) in place of chicken stock I used a 2 chicken soup mix with 8 cups water
Very good and easy to make
Made it as written and it was really tasty. My husband, however, likes things a bit spicier and suggested next time add a little pepper sauce.
Literally delicious and so easy even I couldn’t mess it up!!
Absolutely delicious and easy to prepare. I added diced potatoes and green beans because I wanted more veggies in it.
Just Ok. I found it bland. I would recommend some garlic and more veggies. Instead of crushed tomatoes, consider some fire roasted tomatoes.

Made this for my 36 residents last Saturday for their supper. They loved it and several of them requested seconds. This recipe is delicious, the seasonings are simple, and it is super easy to throw together.
Made it several times. It is delicious.
I thought this dish was boring.
